jobs.title: Legislative Director, Ohio - Columbus
jobs.description_text: Americans for Prosperity (AFP) is the premier grassroots organization focused on advocating solutions to the country’s greatest challenges. We recognize that tens of millions of Americans are frustrated with the extreme partisanship in government that keeps common-sense reforms from being passed, and instead seek to stand with policy leaders who are committed to finding a better way. Americans for Prosperity is part of the Stand Together philanthropic community. As Legislative Director for AFP-Ohio, you'll lead our work at the Ohio Statehouse, serving as our state government affairs lead and lobbyist. You'll track and shape legislation, build trusted relationships with lawmakers and coalition partners, and use AFP's grassroots strength to move policy forward. For this role, the anticipated base salary range is $70,000–$100,000 per year. This role may also be eligible for additional bonus compensation designed to align total compensation with an employee’s overall contribution to the organization.

This role is responsible for ensuring that SRM ballistic performance meets demanding missile-interception requirements while remaining manufacturable at scale. jobs.title: Senior QA Engineer Position for Xsolla's Smart Wallet in Web3
jobs.description_text: ABOUT YOU We are looking for a Senior QA Engineer who has tested real on-chain products — the contracts and the transactions, not only the web app in front of them. You will own quality for Xsolla's smart wallet on Xsolla ZK, our Ethereum-compatible ZK rollup: the wallet players use to hold, receive and send tokens and in-game items, signing in with the account they already have. The work runs on both sides of the chain. On the backend, you will confirm that a wallet address pre-computed from a salt is the address that actually gets deployed. On the frontend, you will follow a signed operation from the client's RPC call through the bundler to finality, and prove it landed, failed or reverted the way it should. You will fork the chain to test against real state, deploy and call contracts from the command line, and turn what you learn into automated suites. You will work in a small, senior engineering team alongside an external wallet-infrastructure partner. You can tell a defect in our code from one in a partner SDK or in the chain itself — and you bring the evidence to show which. AI coding tools are part of how you work every day, and you set them up so the rest of the team gets the same leverage.

Between a system that works on the bench and one that works in the field, the difference is operations: the right kit in the right case, a checklist nobody skips, a manual operators trust. You will take our ground equipment into the field, see first-hand what slows teams down or breaks, and turn every lesson into a lighter kit, a sharper procedure and a better product. Missions Run field deployments: set-up, operation and teardown of ground equipment during trials and deployments. Write operational checklists: preparation, set-up, pre-mission checks and teardown, so every team gets the same result. Organize logistics: transport cases, packing lists, shipping and lithium battery transport. Track weight and portability: weigh each subsystem, set targets with engineering, push for kits that are faster to carry and deploy. Lead verification and validation: test plans, trials, acceptance tests and reports against requirements. Produce user documentation: user manuals, quick-start guides, and structured field feedback to R&D. Required skills Engineering degree or equivalent (systems, mechanical or electronics), with experience in testing, integration or field operations of technical equipment. Strong V&V fundamentals: requirements, test plans, acceptance criteria, test reports. Tools: measurement instruments (multimeter, scales),

jobs.title: Network Engineer – Ground Station Networking & Integration
jobs.description_text: The challenge Our operators rely on a ground network that carries telemetry, video and control between drones, antennas and stations, often set up in minutes on unfamiliar terrain. Networking is what turns separate radios, computers and antennas into one system that behaves the same way on every unit. You will configure and debug on the bench, automate deployments, and troubleshoot live links during field trials. Missions Design the ground network: addressing, routing, switching and power over Ethernet between stations and antenna systems. Integrate telemetry and video flows: MAVLink routing, video streams, latency and reliability measurements. Connect the antenna positioning system to the station: control interface, automatic and manual modes. Automate provisioning: reference images, router configurations, scripts and checklists so every unit is identical. Secure and track deployed systems: workstation hardening, inventory and versions per serial number. Required skills Degree in networking, computer or embedded engineering, with experience in network deployment or embedded systems. Strong IP networking fundamentals: addressing, VLANs, UDP and multicast, latency and packet-loss diagnostics. Tools: Wireshark, router and switch configuration, Windows and Linux, scripting (Python, PowerShell, Bash), Git, Router OS. Clear documentation and cybersecurity basics for sensitive environments. Autonomous and field-oriented, available for frequent travel.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer - Antenna Positioning & Ground Equipment
jobs.description_text: The challenge We build the ground equipment that keeps our interceptor drones connected, and it must be set up fast by a single operator in harsh field conditions. Mechanics decide whether antennas stay on target and whether electronics survive transport, weather and rough handling. You will go from CAD to prototypes to field tests, working hands-on with RF, electrical and operations colleagues. Missions Design an antenna positioning system: drive train, cable management, stiffness and wind resistance. Design rugged enclosures for radio modules and electronics: sealing, thermal management, mounting. Evaluate off-the-shelf solutions: compare commercial positioners and mounts against our needs and support buy-vs-build decisions. Build modularity into the ground equipment: common interfaces, quick set-up, easy maintenance. Take parts from prototype to production: 3D printing to machined parts, drawings, mechanical BOM, assembly instructions. Support field trials and deployments: set-up, feedback from operators, design fixes. Required skills Engineering degree in mechanical or mechatronics engineering, with experience designing electromechanical products. Solid mechanism design fundamentals: tolerancing, gears and reductions, bearings, structural and wind-load calculations. CAD (Fusion 360 or SolidWorks), design for manufacturing and assembly, rapid prototyping (3D printing, CNC). jobs.description_text: Role & Mission Own the development of FPGA functions for our electronic warfare and signals intelligence capabilities, from initial architecture to validation on operational hardware. Work with systems and algorithm engineers to define processing requirements and assess implementation feasibility. Build RTL modules in VHDL or SystemVerilog to process digitized RF signals, extract relevant information, and generate waveforms. Adapt and validate DSP algorithms for FPGA implementation, balancing numerical accuracy, processing speed, and hardware resources. Integrate acquisition and processing chains, including digital down-conversion, filtering, channelization, FFT, detection, direction-finding, and classification. Establish verification methods and testbenches to check functional behavior and performance throughout development. Connect programmable logic to RF converters and embedded processors, defining data transfers, control interfaces, clocking, and synchronization. Resolve implementation constraints, achieve timing closure, and optimize resource utilization and power consumption. Bring up FPGA designs on target boards, investigate integration issues, and correlate measured behavior with simulation results. Contribute to laboratory and field testing alongside RF, software, and systems engineers. Maintain clear design records, interface specifications, and validation evidence. jobs.title: FPGA Engineer - Radar
jobs.description_text: Role & Mission Turn radar sensing requirements into FPGA designs that support reliable drone detection in operational conditions. Define how radar data is acquired, processed, and delivered to the rest of the system, working across RF, electronics, and software teams. Establish processing budgets and select implementation approaches based on detection performance, latency, numerical accuracy, and available FPGA resources. Develop reference models to study radar behavior in noise and clutter and guide hardware design decisions. Build reusable RTL functions for waveform generation and receive processing in FMCW and pulsed radar systems. Implement the processing stages needed to extract targets from radar returns, including matched filtering, pulse compression, range-Doppler processing, clutter rejection, and CFAR detection. Integrate ADC/DAC interfaces, coordinate transmit and receive timing, and ensure synchronization with the radar front end. Specify how detections and associated measurements are passed to tracking functions and embedded software. Verify designs against reference models through automated testbenches and hardware-in-the-loop testing. Investigate performance gaps on target hardware and use laboratory measurements and field results to improve the processing chain. Document design decisions, interfaces, and validation results to support integration and future product development.
